newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine's Kuchma opposes c.bank budget financing.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine's Kuchma opposes c.bank budget financing.

text.p: President Leonid Kuchma told parliament on Friday he opposed financing the government or the economy by the central bank and that fighting inflation should be Ukraine's priority.

"Some circles are persistently promoting the idea of a lack of cash in the state economy and proposing solving urgent economic problems -- including budgetary ones -- on the basis of direct credits," he said.
"The president is decisively and principally opposed to such an approach," he said in his annual state of the nation address.
Kuchma's comments seemed to be addressed at conservatives and industrialists in parliament who want the central bank to pump money into the economy.
Kuchma also said the only way to secure economic growth was to halve inflation this year and in 1998 and he said the budget deficit needed to be cut and not financed by the central bank.

"Ukraine's strategic goal is to cover the state budget deficit without using any direct credits as soon as possible and to cut the deficit to a level which does not exceed three percent of gross domestic product," Kuchma said.
A forecast issued to deputies and obtained by Reuters said Ukraine should aim to achieve annual inflation of 20-25 percent this year and 10-12 percent in 1998.
Annual inflation fell to 39.7 percent last year from 181.7 percent in 1995 and 10,225 percent in 1993.

The International Monetary Fund is talking to Ukraine about a long-term, $2.5-$3 billion Extended Fund Facility loan but parliament must first pass this year's budget and a package of tax reforms to underpin it. --Kiev newsroom +38-044-229-2264
